checks.why: a handler under a type prefix is served at the composed route only: a bare "/login" in a security rule or a string array is not a request for /auth/login, and the request that sends /auth/login is
a one-segment template under a prefix (/logs/{ids}) is not matched by every one-segment path in the tree, nor by a /** pattern
near miss: a route with no type prefix is still joined to the request that sends it, and not to the security rule that names the same path
control: a path held in a constant outside any call, then sent, still reaches its handler
